Rewrote the `__init__` for clarity
Rewrote the `generateDerivatives` function to be split into multiple function with more comments and more clarity.

Removed normalization from metric function and instead normalize before the finite differences. A flag for the user has been added for it. Additionally, the makePos flag now only makes the properties all positive when reordering, instead of overwriting the sign of the original data.
Added more descriptive text to argparse
fixed functionality for alternate sweep, added formatting changes, and added the ability to sort the states by energies at the last or first point in the point range
fixed setting offset to allow for the starting point to be swapped
Made the formatting of the figure consistent so that way updates to the figure looks the same as its initialization.
Added ability to choose whether to sort the states by the energies at the first point or at the last point.
instead of toggling a checkbox, there are separate buttons for sweeping forwards, backwards, and alternating between the two.
Decided to normalize the finite differences of the properties by default. They are not as important as the energies.
moved the code for the gui into a separate file (after brushing up on modularization in python; would have done it sooner)
Bad typo for finding states to use in finite differences.
Now preventing points from outside the `pntBounds` to contribute to the finite differences. Also made optimization for finding states to use in finite differences.
The starting point does not effectively swap states when `futurePnts = 0`. If the current point is the starting point, now we set `futurePnts = 1` if it was not already greater than zero.

Changed functionality of `stateBounds` to prevent states outside of the state bounds from swapping with states inside the state bounds. This may potential be added as a flag for the user to determine.
updated definition for `getMetric` and changed description of `stateBounds` functionality
new definition for `getMetric`.
Better indicates the location of the file to modify the `getMetric` function.
The `getMetric` function for swapping states has been a difficulty for getting smooth curves. The function has been moved to a separate file where the user may modify it for their use case.
sum with axis does not work properly with numba. This has been a vital mistake.

Properties are normalized to reduce their importance during reordering. This should take in a parameter in a later commit. Also, a weight may be good to add to further reduce the importance of properties.

Changed method for calculating the metric for swapping states. Logarithms should not have been used to reduce the magnitude of metric, and numba had not performed the reduction of the properties tensor like intended. This gave drastically inaccurate reorderings.

Additionally, many variable names have been refactored.

Added a slider for selecting which properties to use in the finite difference calculations.

Added more tools to use in interactive mode.
Had a few mistakes with creating the validArray. Now resolved.
program had crashed when shuffling energies without a defined point bound.
It's better to allow nans to swap with each other when not interpolating points now that I have the derivatives being interpolated.

A LONG needed functionality has finally been implemented.

 Using Dash and plotly, this script can now spawn an interactive plot embedded in a local browser. This allows one to visualize the entire reordering procedure and manipulated the algorithm by interacting with the interface.

 This drastically improves the usability of this tool and diminishes troubleshooting time.
Moving states after they have been sorted is not a great idea...
Default handling of invalid points without interpolating values is to instead interpolate nan derivatives with the previous value.
Sorting was causing mistakes because it was done after creating the stateMap. Restored invalid derivatives to being the mean derivative
Updated stateMap as a global variable and now will move invalid points to the last state by default when not interpolating.
Added check if validArray needs to be evaluated.
changed default fill value for invalid points to max finite difference.

Sorting states when dealing with invalid points drastically diminishes the accuracy. Instead, the states are sorted by energy when printed out, but is left unsorted during the reordering process.

Also improved checks for invalid points and default set them to the average derivative of all states to have them ignored.

Made a few oversights for certain settings in the configuration file when it comes to dealing with invalid points.

Now, any nans or infs that show up in the finite differences are just set to zero.

Made another algorithm for dealing with invalid points by simply ignoring them when calculating finite differences.

Added some more parameters for interpolating invalid points and will now do so for each state instead of for each sweep.
Made another algorithm for dealing with invalid points by simply ignoring them when calculating finite differences
Added an eWidth parameter that only allows the current state to swap with nearby energy states.
Fixed issue with setting lobound for states improperly when allowing redundant swaps.

Major refactoring of the code to encapsulate all functions into a class (except the numba functions).

This makes the script more portable for use in other python projects instead of as just a standalone script. In addition, I have allowed for the getMetric function to be a class variable which can be overwritten by the user to define their own loss function for the reordering procedure.

(All these changes should have been done long ago really. Ideally from the start. Would have made both my life and your life easier...)
